positions.name: ReadinessStandardWarrant
positions.frame: how does a leader's directive get warranted by casting an unrehearsed capability as no capability at all?
positions.why: src-1 issues the monthly cadence directive; src-2 supplies the aphoristic warrant — an unrehearsed rollback is one we do not have; src-3 renders both in reported speech, carrying the principal's stance through another's quotation. The same directional read spans all three: authority claims its mandate by declaring a readiness standard, not by rank alone. Tension between the directive's forward-looking cadence and the maxim's present-tense counterfactual is held — the rule warrants the schedule.

positions.name: DirectiveAsOperationalMetadata
positions.frame: how is an imposed cadence recorded as a standing operational fact through structured metadata?
positions.why: src-4 restates the cadence as a labeled field; src-5 assigns ownership to the named principal. Both perform the same move: ratifying the directive as settled operational record, converting a spoken mandate into a fixed artifact.
